chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I went to pelt (the Jamarah), and I found six pebbles in my hand.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Take one from beneath your foot.'

key_terms.أَرْمِي: I pelt (referring to the Hajj ritual of throwing pebbles at the Jamarah)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they have an incorrect number of pebbles during the Rami ritual?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *takhfif* (ease) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects a minor discrepancy in the number of pebbles used for Rami. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on precision in ritual acts while allowing for practical adjustments, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills the obligation without undue hardship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘ I went over to pelt, but there were six pebbles in my hand’. So heasws said: ‘Take one from beneath your foot (but not from the Jamarah as per above Ahadith)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:
“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I went to throw pebbles but there were only six pebbles in my hand.’ He (the Imam) said, ’Take one from under your feet.’”
